syllabusTopics: Biomolecules: Introduction and functions of carbohydrates, proteins, lipids, nucleic acids, minerals, enzymes and water
Cell: Introduction of cell, concepts of prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells

Detail structure of eukaryotic cells: cell wall, cell membrane, mitochondria, plastids, endoplasmic reticulum, golgi bodies, lysosomes, ribosomes, nucleus, chromosomes, cilia, flagella and cell inclusions
Cell division: Concept of cell cycle, types of cell division (amitosis, mitosis and meiosis) and significances

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Cells come from cells. Prokaryotes keep a nucleoid and 70S ribosomes. Eukaryotes add a nucleus, mitochondria, and, in green cells, chloroplasts, plus ER, Golgi, lysosomes and 80S ribosomes. Plants add a cellulose wall that animals do not have.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Cell theory: living things are made of cells, the cell is the unit of structure and function, and cells arise from cells.
A prokaryotic cell has a nucleoid, 70S ribosomes and no mitochondria. A eukaryotic cell has a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Animal cells have no cellulose wall.  ·  80S ribosomes are eukaryotic. 70S are prokaryotic, and also inside mitochondria.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: The cell membrane is fluid mosaic model – a dynamic arrangement of lipids and proteins.  ·  Mitochondrial DNA is circular and similar to bacterial DNA, supporting endosymbiotic theory.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: The plasma membrane is a selective boundary. The cell wall, in plants, is outside it and is cellulose. Animal cells have no cellulose wall.

rows.text: Cell membrane is selectively permeable – small molecules diffuse freely, large molecules need carriers.  ·  Mitochondria = powerhouse of the cell (produces ATP).

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Cell theory has three postulates: 1) All living things are made of cells, 2) Cells are the basic unit of structure/function, 3) New cells come from existing cells.  ·  Organelle function questions commonly appear – match organelle to its primary function.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Cell membrane: selectively permeable phospholipid bilayer  ·  Nucleus: controls cell activities, contains DNA  ·  Mitochondria: powerhouse of the cell (ATP production)  ·  Ribosomes: protein synthesis machinery (70S in prokaryotes, 80S in eukaryotes)

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Organelles have specific functions: nucleus (control), mitochondria (energy), ER (synthesis), Golgi (packaging), lysosomes (digestion).  ·  Prokaryotic cells lack membrane-bound organelles but have a nucleoid region with DNA.  ·  Eukaryotic cells have a true nucleus surrounded by a nuclear envelope.  ·  Cells come from cells.

rows.text: Why do mitochondria have their own DNA?  ·  What is the difference between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells?

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Mitochondria release energy by aerobic respiration and carry a little of their own DNA. Chloroplasts, in green cells, do the same kind of semi-independent life for photosynthesis.  ·  Rough endoplasmic reticulum carries ribosomes and helps make proteins. The Golgi body packages secretions. Lysosomes hold digestive enzymes. Ribosomes, 80S in the eukaryotic cytosol, build proteins.  ·  The nucleus holds the chromosomes. Cilia and flagella move a cell or the fluid past it. Vacuoles and stored granules are inclusions, not the same thing as an organelle with a job in metabolism.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Endoplasmic reticulum: RER (protein synthesis), SER (lipid synthesis)  ·  Golgi apparatus: modification, sorting, and packaging of proteins/lipids  ·  Lysosomes: digestive compartments containing hydrolytic enzymes

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Chloroplasts: site of photosynthesis (plant cells only)  ·  Centrosome: organizes microtubules in animal cells  ·  Nucleoid versus nucleus.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Mitochondria and chloroplasts.  ·  ER, Golgi, lysosome, ribosome.  ·  A lysosome is not the nucleus.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Inclusions are storage. Organelles do the metabolic work.  ·  Chloroplasts contain thylakoids where light-dependent reactions occur.  ·  Order in a sequence is part of the answer.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Do not call a timberline a snowline.  ·  The cell membrane regulates what enters and exits the cell via passive and active transport.  ·  Mitochondria generate ATP through oxidative phosphorylation in the electron transport chain.
